repos.name: up-bootstrap
repos.info: The cloud-account setup repo — the foundational, account-level concerns everything else depends on. Three modules: rbac (global — the eight platform-team Entra groups, PIM policies, operator managed identities with OIDC-federated credentials for runners), setup (per sector-tier resource-group creation), audit (PIM-activation alerts + the central Log Analytics — the audit trail of WHO elevated and when). Team membership is one members.yml (admins/contributors/readers by email). Levels: admins → Owner (PIM, 8 h + justification), contributors → Contributor + RBAC Administrator (PIM), operators → permanent Owner (CI managed identities only, no humans), readers → permanent Reader.

repos.name: up-identity
repos.info: Extended, ad-hoc Entra ID groups defined in YAML — access grants beyond a tenant's defaults. This is where a user of ANOTHER tenant receives permissions (e.g. a data-qa or storage-reader group per environment): one config file per group, named {tenant}-{domain}-{purpose}, members listed by email, deployed by CI with SAST/IaC/secret scans on every MR.

repos.name: up-tenants
repos.info: Defines what a TENANT gets: seven Entra groups ({tenant}-live/sandbox-admins/contributors/operators + {tenant}-readers) plus the tenant's resource groups per region, Key Vaults, Terraform state containers and {tenant}-{tier}-operator managed identities for CI. Levels: admins → Contributor + User Access Administrator + KV Secrets Officer (PIM, 8 h, justification); contributors → Contributor + KV Secrets Officer (PIM); operators → permanent (service accounts only, no humans); readers → permanent Reader, no Key Vault.

repos.name: up-storage-proxy
repos.info: Data-plane access instead of standing credentials: a managed-identity proxy that scopes every storage request per-call — no long-lived SAS tokens, one revocation point.

repos.name: up-kubernetes
repos.info: A different permission plane: IN-CLUSTER Kubernetes RBAC. AKS authenticates users via Entra ID with Azure RBAC disabled — ClusterRoleBindings map the bootstrap groups onto Kubernetes roles (platform contributors → cluster-admin, platform readers → view). The cluster's own managed identity additionally gets Reader on the subscription and Network Contributor on the VNet/NSGs.

repos.name: up-namespaces
repos.info: Namespace-scoped Kubernetes RBAC + guardrails: every application namespace gets four role bindings bound to the tenant's Entra groups (admins → ClusterRole admin; contributors → custom Role, everything except RBAC; operators → admin for CI; readers → custom Role, no secrets) plus ResourceQuotas, LimitRanges and prevent_destroy. A namespace is one YAML file declaring its tenant and the clusters it deploys to — the tenant-level counterpart to up-kubernetes' cluster-wide bindings.

repos.name: up-gitlab-tenants
repos.info: GitLab-side permissions: creates each tenant's GitLab group, assigns role-based memberships for tenant owners, and — behind a per-tenant runners flag — provisions Kubernetes-native CI runners. Auth chain: runner pod → K8s ServiceAccount → workload-identity federated credential → the tenant's {tenant}-{tier}-operator identity (owned by up-tenants) → tenant resource groups. No long-lived secrets anywhere.

repos.name: up-grafana-tenants
repos.info: Grafana-side permissions — one for_each over the tenant YAMLs: per tenant a team, an isolated folder and a viewer service account for tooling. Access matrix: platform team → Admin everywhere; every other team → Edit its own folder, View the rest (deliberate cross-tenant visibility). Per-tenant alerts + dashboards deploy from JSON via shared modules. Users must already exist in Grafana — no user sync.

repos.name: up-backups
repos.info: Centralized backup management: two Data Protection + two Recovery Services vaults per (sector, tier, region) — a GeoZone-redundant pair for critical data (cross-region restore) and a Zone-redundant pair for important data. Enrolment is tag-driven: DINE policies auto-enrol disks/VMs tagged data_criticality=important|critical; scheduled daily jobs discover and enrol database servers and storage accounts; an AKS extension backs up label-opted-in PVCs. Trunk-based with a canary tuple + automated smoke test gating auto-promotion to the remaining tuples. Vault is additive — built-in PITR / soft-delete remain the primary recovery path.

Tool-agnostic (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, GPT/Gemini tools); distributed as a Claude Code plugin so its skills are available in every session. This is the how-we-work-with-AI layer; the ai/ repos are the infrastructure that work travels through.

repos.name: ai-foundry
repos.info: STATUS: scaffold in review — main is EMPTY; the scaffold MR (Foundry account, project and model deployments) is unmerged; nothing deployed. WHAT THE CODE DECLARES: one shared AI Foundry account (ultracore-eu01), no sandbox/live split, with six GPT-5.x deployments in the tfvars — the map key IS the deployment name clients would pass in the model field. Applies run serial; outputs are consumed by ai-gateway via remote state. The Claude backend for agentic dev is NOT here — it lives in ai-gateway's own Sweden Central account.

repos.name: ai-gateway
repos.info: STATUS: scaffold in review — main is EMPTY; the redesign MR (Foundry remote state, split policies, subscription management) is unmerged; nothing deployed by CI, PoC applies are manual + torn down. WHAT THE CODE DECLARES: an API Management GenAI gateway (sandbox Basic v2, no VNet; live Standard v2, VNet-integrated) with exactly ONE API — Claude (Anthropic Messages API) at path ai/claude — backed by claude-sonnet-4-6 in the gateway's OWN Foundry account in Sweden Central (managed identity; enable_foundry=false falls back to the api.anthropic.com passthrough if subscription eligibility blocks Foundry Claude). Policies: llm-token-limit (50k/100k TPM per personal key, 429 + Retry-After), llm-emit-token-metric → App Insights. The OpenAI-compatible /llm/v1 facade for applications is designed, NOT in code yet. Next milestone: Entra ID SSO.

repos.name: ai-subscriptions
repos.info: STATUS: scaffold in review — main is EMPTY; the scaffold MR (subscription key provisioning) is unmerged; nothing deployed; depends on ai-gateway remote state, so it can only apply after ai-gateway does. DESIGN: one gateway subscription key per application in subscriptions.yaml ({name, display_name, team}); merge auto-applies; retrieve with `terraform output -json subscription_keys`; share via the secrets manager — never chat or email. Client gotcha: pass the key as default_headers={'Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key': key} in the OpenAI SDK — the gateway ignores Authorization: Bearer.
